claims.text: Nanometer-scale compositional inhomogeneities create local strain fields in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Local strain fields enhance magnetoelastic coupling at phase boundaries.
The tailored microstructure promotes reversible magnetic reorientations under low applied fields.
Reversible low-field magnetic reorientations produce a strong magnetocaloric response.
The tailored microstructure preserves rapid heat exchange and mechanical stability.
Arc-melted and thermally treated high-entropy-alloy samples typically have an interpenetrating microstructure with nanoscale chemical heterogeneities.
Changing the concentration of a minor alloying element can alter lattice-parameter mismatch.
Changing lattice-parameter mismatch alters the intensity of local strain fields.
Nanoscale local strain fields at compositional phase boundaries mediate magnetoelastic interactions.
Enhanced magnetoelastic coupling at phase boundaries enables low-field triggering of reversible magnetic phase transitions.
Reversible magnetic phase transitions increase the magnetocaloric effect while minimizing hysteresis.
An ultrafine interconnected grain structure supports rapid heat exchange.
An ultrafine interconnected grain structure maintains mechanical integrity.
Relative to the baseline, the compositionally modified alloy should have a shifted magnetic transition temperature.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy should exhibit a larger low-field adiabatic temperature-change peak.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy should exhibit reduced hysteresis loss.
The modified alloy should maintain hardness and tensile stability relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism should apply only while nanoscale compositional inhomogeneities and their associated strain fields are maintained.
Significant changes in processing or alloy system may produce behavior governed by a different mechanism.
